display: Dale Whitcombe, a wild mushroom foraging guide in Victoria, BC. After 15 years in forestry I now lead small-group walks on southern Vancouver Island: chanterelles in fall, morels in spring. I get a steady stream of Mandarin inquiries and want to launch Mandarin-language tours in spring 2027.

signals.text: I keep getting Mandarin emails and WeChat messages asking for a Chinese-speaking foraging guide, and I keep having to say no. That is three times this month.
I want to launch Mandarin-language walks in spring 2027, starting with early morels around April, but I haven't worked out who would guide them.
Half the Asian cruise-ship tourists on my walks ask about matsutake, and we only get a few. I need an honest way to handle that.
On my last walk, two couples from Taipei were whispering about whether to eat what we found. I wish I could have explained the real ID details in their language.
A Vancouver tour operator asked about a group of 12 retired teachers from Shanghai. I had to say English only for now and keep in touch.
I can't offer tasting on walks because my insurance doesn't clearly cover it. My broker wants a written protocol with a species list, an ID method and a named sign-off.
My own ID skill is solid, but it is one person's opinion. I need a mycologist willing to review and co-sign an ID protocol.
I'm looking for a way to turn the Mandarin interest into bookings and not leave it at 'next year'. Spring 2027 is six months away.
Park permit applications open November 1, and I have to log my harvest numbers.
My cabin deck rebuild is behind schedule and the joists are sitting under a tarp. Rain delays and the cost are both a drag.
Last year's cider went flat by March. This year I have 60 litres in the carboy and would like advice on keeping it from stalling.
I'm tired after a heavy season of weekend walks, long drives and not enough field bags. It has been a good year, though.
Income drops sharply from January to March, and I want an off-season line of work.
I worry about a poisoning claim if a client eats something wrong, and that worry is why I haven't moved faster on tasting.

offers.text: Small-group guided foraging walks, six at a time and capped at eight, on southern Vancouver Island, with a hot field lunch.
Nine years of guiding and about 1,100 clients. I know 40+ edible species well, with a field ID set and a pressed spore-print collection.
Commercial guiding permits for four provincial and regional park areas near Sooke and Port Renfrew.
A client email list of about 2,300 and a website with a booking calendar, which could carry a launch announcement.
A 2017 Ford Transit with seats for eight and a gear trailer, for ground transport on tours.
First Aid Level 3 and a wilderness first responder ticket.
Fifteen years in forestry, including timber cruising and tree planting. I can read forest terrain, land and access.
Home cider pressing with a hand press, and field soup for groups (lentil and chorizo, three litres at a time).
A relationship with Vancouver tour operators who already send Mandarin-speaking group inquiries.

catchers.hypo: I'm a Mandarin-English bilingual who loves mushrooms and the outdoors. Would you want a co-guide or interpreter for Mandarin walks next spring?
catchers.can: Trial them as an interpreter or co-guide on spring 2027 walks, train them on species and safety, and set up a paid or revenue-share arrangement.
catchers.confirm: Are you fluent in spoken Mandarin and comfortable with a full day outdoors on uneven forest ground, up to six hours of walking?

catchers.hypo: I run tours out of Vancouver for Chinese-speaking groups. I have 12 retired teachers from Shanghai who want a foraging experience on the Island. Can you host them in Mandarin?
catchers.can: Run the walk in spring or fall with an interpreter, in groups of eight or fewer. Dale can arrange transport in his van and work out pricing.
catchers.confirm: Can your group be split into parties of eight or fewer per guide, and will it travel in the April-to-October season?

catchers.hypo: I'm visiting from Taiwan in October and would love to find matsutake. Can you guide me, and in Chinese?
catchers.can: Be honest that matsutake are scarce. Offer a chanterelle walk now, or put them on the Mandarin list for 2027 with an interpreter.
catchers.confirm: Are you happy to go on a walk where matsutake are possible but not guaranteed, and do you understand you must not eat anything the guide hasn't confirmed?

catchers.hypo: I'm a mycologist at a university or a mushroom society. I could review an ID protocol for commercial foraging tours and sign off on it.
catchers.can: Write the species list, ID method and sign-off into a documented protocol, which is what Dale's insurance broker asked for before any tasting.
catchers.confirm: Are you a practising mycologist or credentialed ID expert for Pacific Northwest edible species, willing to put your name on a written protocol?

catchers.hypo: I'm an insurance broker who writes cover for outdoor-guide businesses. I've covered wild-food tours with a documented ID protocol before.
catchers.can: Compare cover options for tasting on tours and learn what protocol the underwriter needs, so Dale can decide whether Mandarin tasting walks are viable.
catchers.confirm: Have you actually placed liability cover for tours where clients eat foraged wild mushrooms, in Canada?

catchers.hypo: I'm a nurse educator and we want a short talk on wild mushroom poisoning for hospital or health-unit staff.
catchers.can: Dale can give a practical talk on look-alikes and safe ID. He can also reach nursing colleagues through his wife, who works as a nurse at a Victoria hospital.
catchers.confirm: Is this an educational talk on safe identification and look-alikes, and not a request for medical diagnosis or treatment advice?

catchers.hypo: I have an apple tree and don't know what to do with the fruit. I'd love someone to press it or teach me to make cider.
catchers.can: Connect them with Howard, Dale's neighbour and cider partner, to share pressing and fermentation experience.
catchers.confirm: Do you have at least 50 kg of apples within driving distance of Sooke, and are you open to sharing the cider?

catchers.hypo: I'm a Mandarin-speaking student or translator in Victoria. I'd love a weekend field gig and I'd like to learn about wild food.
catchers.can: Bring them on as a paid or in-kind interpreter on fall or spring walks, and teach them species and safety.
catchers.confirm: Are you available on weekends in the fall or spring, and comfortable with long walks in the forest and with translating safety instructions?

catchers.hypo: I run a cruise or tourism business bringing Asian visitors to Victoria. I want to add a nature-based half-day with a licensed local guide.
catchers.can: Add a scheduled walk of eight or fewer guests with a hot lunch, with Mandarin support from spring 2027.
catchers.confirm: Can your guests be split into groups of eight or fewer and travel about an hour to Sooke or Port Renfrew?

forbids.text: Groups are capped at eight, because the permits allow no more.
I don't guide in the heat of August.
I won't offer tasting on walks without proper insurance cover and a documented ID protocol.
I won't confirm or tell clients to eat any wild mushroom I haven't identified myself.
I can't run walks every weekend, and Sundays in winter are family time.
I only guide in the four permitted areas near Sooke and Port Renfrew, not elsewhere on the Island.
I limit steep descents on long routes.
I don't currently guide in Mandarin and won't claim to until there is a qualified guide or interpreter.

projects.name: Mandarin-language foraging tours, spring 2027
projects.text: Launch Mandarin tours around April for early morels, and fold in chanterelles in the fall. Open questions: who guides, how to handle tasting, and what insurance allows.
roles_needed: Insurance broker with experience of tasting cover
Mandarin-speaking tour operator or marketing partner (WeChat)

projects.name: Documented ID and tasting protocol
projects.text: A written protocol with a species list, ID method and named sign-off, to satisfy the insurer so tasting can be offered safely.

policy.t1: When there is a real lead, share group sizes, pricing, permits, and the insurance and ID-protocol hurdles.
policy.t2: Once trust is high and the other party is clear, share the seasonal income gaps in winter and my personal concerns about poisoning risk.
policy.never: My home address, family medical details, and any health information about me or my family.
